name: complex-geometry
title: Complex geometry: Stokes flow through a porous pillar lattice
question:
Does a real gmsh-constructed periodic array of circular pillars --
imported into dolfinx via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh` -- support a
genuine steady Stokes (creeping) flow solve, driven by a prescribed
pressure drop, that stays approximately divergence-free and exactly
no-slip on every pillar and channel wall, and does the effective (Darcy)
permeability computed from that flow DECREASE monotonically as the
lattice's porosity decreases -- the Kozeny-Carman-type physical trend
expected of any real porous microstructure?
hypothesis:
A real Taylor-Hood (P2 velocity / P1 pressure) mixed dolfinx solve on the
gmsh-generated pillar-lattice mesh, driven by a "do-nothing"
pressure-boundary-load formulation (no-slip on walls+pillars, pressure
prescribed only as a natural momentum-equation load at the open
inflow/outflow boundaries -- see `viva_fenics/processes/flow.py`'s module
comment above `PorousFlowStep`), should produce a physically valid
creeping-flow field on every lattice density tried, and the
volume-averaged x-velocity this field produces -- fed through Darcy's law
-- should fall as the pillar packing gets denser (porosity drops),
matching the qualitative Kozeny-Carman scaling (k ~ phi^3/(1-phi)^2) even
though a 4-point sweep cannot independently validate that scaling's exact
exponents.
objective:
Build the `porous_lattice` composite (a single `PorousFlowStep`: gmsh
pillar-lattice geometry construction -> dolfinx Taylor-Hood import ->
steady Stokes solve -> Darcy permeability) for a baseline porosity plus 3
porosity variants (sweeping `pillar_radius` at fixed 4x4 lattice density)
and verify (a) every solve is approximately divergence-free and exactly
no-slip on every pillar/wall boundary, and (b) the effective permeability
k_eff decreases monotonically as porosity decreases across all 4 points.
description:
Wraps a single `PorousFlowStep` in the `porous_lattice` composite
generator. The Step is stateless -- given only a pillar-lattice
configuration (grid size, pillar radius, mesh grading, viscosity,
pressure drop), it: (1) builds the geometry with the real gmsh Python API
(`viva_fenics.fem_gmsh.build_porous_lattice_mesh`) -- a unit channel
rectangle with an nx-by-ny grid of circular pillars boolean-cut out
(`gmsh.model.occ`), with 4 tagged boundary groups (inflow/outflow/
walls/pillars) and a mesh graded finer at every pillar boundary than in
the open channel interior; (2) imports the resulting unstructured
triangulation into a dolfinx Taylor-Hood MIXED function space (P2 vector
velocity / P1 scalar pressure, one `basix.ufl.mixed_element`, following
the dolfinx 0.11 Stokes demo's `mixed_direct()` pattern); and (3) solves
the steady Stokes equations (-div(2*mu*epsilon(u) - p*I) = 0, div(u) = 0)
with no-slip velocity on the channel walls and EVERY pillar, and the
pressure drop imposed as a "do-nothing" natural boundary LOAD (not a
Dirichlet constraint on the pressure space -- see the module comment
above `PorousFlowStep` for why the more naive Dirichlet-pressure
formulation was tried first and found to drive ~zero net flow) at the
open inflow/outflow boundaries. A SINGLE linear saddle-point
`dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` solve produces the full field -- no
time-stepping, since creeping flow has no unsteady term.

The effective (Darcy) permeability is then read directly off the solved
field: k_eff = mu * <u_x> * L / delta_p, where <u_x> is the real
FEM-assembled volume average of the x-velocity over the fluid domain (not
a nodal average) and L is the channel length. Porosity itself is also a
real FEM-assembled reading (fluid-area fraction of the imported mesh, not
the closed-form geometry estimate -- see `fem_gmsh.build_porous_lattice_
mesh`'s docstring for why the two only approximately agree).

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study: it turns the investigation's
earlier "Poisson on a gmsh hole" demonstration into a genuine porous-media
engineering result -- a real creeping-flow solve on a periodic
microstructure, with a physically meaningful derived quantity (effective
permeability) that varies correctly with the medium's geometry, not just
a bounded scalar field.

expected_behavior.name: stokes-flow-divergence-free-and-noslip
expected_behavior.en: On every one of the 4 porosities, the steady Stokes solve produces a velocity field with small mean |div(u)| (approximately divergence-free -- Taylor-Hood is an LBB-stable pairing, much closer to exact incompressibility than the IPCS operator splitting used elsewhere in this investigation) AND exactly zero velocity (to solver precision) on every no-slip (wall + pillar) boundary dof.
expected_behavior.condition: max(divergence_mean across variants) < 1e-2 and max(noslip_max_speed across variants) < 1e-8
expected_behavior.rationale: A real Taylor-Hood mixed Stokes solve with correctly-applied no-slip Dirichlet BCs should satisfy both properties essentially exactly (up to discretization/solver tolerance); a large divergence residual or a nonzero no-slip speed would indicate a broken mesh import, a misclassified boundary group, or an incorrectly assembled saddle-point system.

expected_behavior.name: permeability-decreases-with-porosity
expected_behavior.en: The effective (Darcy) permeability k_eff DECREASES monotonically as porosity decreases across the 4-point sweep (sparse -> medium -> baseline -> dense), matching the qualitative Kozeny-Carman-type trend expected of a real porous microstructure.
expected_behavior.condition: k_eff(porosity_i) > k_eff(porosity_i+1) for every consecutive pair, sorted by porosity descending
expected_behavior.rationale: Darcy's law relates volume-averaged flow to permeability at fixed driving pressure drop; a denser pillar packing leaves less open pore space for the fluid to move through, so at the SAME pressure drop the volume-averaged velocity -- and hence k_eff -- must fall as porosity falls. A non-monotonic or flat trend would indicate the porosity sweep isn't actually changing the flow resistance (e.g. a geometry-generation bug where pillar_radius silently has no effect).

behavior_tests.name: mesh-imports-with-tagged-boundaries
behavior_tests.description:
n_cells (the imported dolfinx mesh's local cell count) for EVERY one of
the 4 porosity variants must exceed 20, and every boundary facet group
(inflow/outflow/walls/pillars) must be non-empty (checked directly in
tests/test_complex_geometry.py; this run's floor is a coarse sanity
check on the same underlying mesh-import path).

provenance.note: Observed cell counts at nx=ny=4, h_pillar=0.015 run 5000-9000 across the porosity sweep (see studies/complex-geometry/sims/run.py's printed summary); 20 is a generous floor that only fails on a genuinely degenerate/empty import.

behavior_tests.name: stokes-flow-divergence-free-and-noslip
behavior_tests.description:
For every one of the 4 porosities, the Stokes solve's mean |div(u)|
must stay below 1e-2 (approximately divergence-free) AND the max speed
over every no-slip boundary dof must stay below 1e-8 (exact no-slip to
solver precision).

provenance.note: Observed mean|div(u)| at production resolution runs 3e-5-1e-4 across the porosity sweep (a real Taylor-Hood LBB-stable pairing is much closer to exact incompressibility than this investigation's IPCS processes) -- 1e-2 leaves two orders of magnitude of headroom while still catching a genuinely broken assembly.

behavior_tests.name: noslip-satisfied-on-pillars
behavior_tests.description:
Max speed over every no-slip (wall + pillar) boundary dof must stay
below 1e-8 across all 4 porosities -- confirms the Dirichlet BC landed
on the real tagged pillar facets, not silently skipped or misapplied to
the wrong boundary group.

provenance.note: Dirichlet BC dof elimination zeroes these dofs to machine precision by construction; observed max is exactly 0.0 in development runs, a 1e-8 floor leaves comfortable headroom for solver round-off while still catching a genuinely leaked/unapplied BC.

behavior_tests.name: permeability-decreases-with-porosity
behavior_tests.description:
The effective permeability k_eff must be finite and strictly positive
at every porosity, AND must decrease monotonically (every consecutive
pair, sorted by porosity descending) across the 4-point sweep -- the
headline Kozeny-Carman-type physical trend this study exists to
demonstrate.

provenance.note: Darcy's law at fixed driving pressure drop: a denser pillar packing leaves less open pore space, so the volume-averaged velocity (and hence k_eff) must fall as porosity falls -- see this study's expected_behavior for the full argument. The observed 4-point sweep shows a >10x drop in k_eff from the sparsest to the densest lattice (see studies/complex-geometry/sims/run.py's printed summary for the exact achieved values).

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
complex-geometry; it is the investigation's porous-media/Stokes-flow
showcase, built directly on the validated dolfinx bridge
(poisson-validation) rather than on the scalar diffusion/reaction
studies -- it needs a correct FEM solve, not the transient stores this
investigation's other advanced studies build on.
